text.p: Italian debt markets held in firmer territory ahead of the results of the FOMC meeting at which the U.S. Federal Reserve was widely expected to tighten monetary policy.

Brokers noted a rumour in late trade that a U.S. consultancy had issued a report saying the Fed would not tighten. The runour helped push bond markets up but while the consultants neither confirmed or denied the talk, subscribers said no such report had been issued. Brokers said now, with investors expecting a pre-emptive move, no action might have a negative effect on debt markets.
The November 2006 Btp ended 76 basis points higher at 100.95, yielding 7.72 percent and showing a spread over the benchmark Bund of 185 basis points.
The June future on LIFFE was 75 basis points up at 125.25 while the lira was hanging in at 1,001.65/1.95 per mark, little changed from late on Monday.

Brokers said the market was in wait and see mode for the Fed but also because it wanted to see the measures the Italian government would take in the mini-budget it is expected to unveil later this week, with Prime Minister Romano Prodi saying it would be done before Easter.
Sources said the package should be approved by the Italian cabinet on Thursday or Friday. Brokers say they doubt the measures will contain any significant structural changes.

Prodi also said Italy was not seeking a delay in European economic and monetary union, after foreign minister Lamberto Dini said earlier a one year EMU postponement would be useful but impossible to negotiate at this stage.
